public_rationale: Marcus said margins on serving tokens were very slim or negative in many cases. Part of this holds. TechCrunch reported in April 2026 that Cursor, like many AI-coding startups, had run at negative gross margins until recently. It had only reached slight gross profitability, and it still lost money on individual developer accounts. But Anthropic's S-1 shows an implied 85% gross margin for the first half of 2026, up from about 12% a year earlier. So a leading model provider was not running slim or negative serving margins overall in this period. The claim fits app-layer coding tools and flat-price individual plans. It does not fit the aggregate margins of at least one major LLM provider.
limitations: The 85% figure is a headline figure from the S-1. Its cost of revenue may leave out some serving costs, such as free-tier compute.
No verified OpenAI margin data was available.
Which companies count as 'these companies' affects the result.

our_interpretation: 'Here' refers to companies serving AI tokens through flat-price, all-you-can-eat subscriptions and agent use, including model providers and AI coding products.
Plain reading: in the months before the post, many such companies, or many of their plans and customer segments, had very slim or negative gross margins on serving usage.
'In many cases' is a hedge. Negative margins in some significant segments count toward support. A strong positive aggregate gross margin at a leading provider counts against the broad picture.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reporting or filings show gross margins near zero or negative for token-serving AI companies, or for major plans or customer segments, during roughly March to June 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible filings show that the main providers had healthy gross margins on serving usage in that period, leaving few slim or negative cases.
